subject.title: refactor(meeting-bot): extract browser meeting-bot core behind MeetingPlatformAdapter

question: Should OpenClaw commit the proposed broad `openclaw/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime` API now, or keep most meeting machinery internal until a second platform adapter proves the reusable contract?
rationale: The branch introduces a permanent external plugin surface with 81 exports and 32 callables; tests can validate implementation behavior but cannot decide the intended long-term compatibility boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrower stable API
options.body: Keep the adapter and essential runtime entrypoints public, but trim implementation-oriented helpers that the upcoming Teams adapter does not demonstrably need.

options.title: Keep it internal for now
options.body: Land the core extraction without a public SDK subpath, then publish the smallest proven contract alongside the second adapter.

options.title: Accept the full surface
options.body: Approve all proposed exports as supported plugin API and own their future compatibility and deprecation requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrower stable API
recommendation.body: Keep the adapter and essential runtime entrypoints public, but trim implementation-oriented helpers that the upcoming Teams adapter does not demonstrably need.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows sustained ownership of the preceding voice-stack consolidation and the concrete requirements driving this API.
